questions.question: A Lambda function must write to one DynamoDB table. What is the most secure way to grant access?
options: An execution role allowing PutItem on that table only
An access key stored in an environment variable
A resource policy allowing any principal
questions.correct_rationale: Execution roles give temporary credentials scoped to the one action and table needed.

questions.domain: 1. Designing and Planning a Google Cloud Network
questions.question: A financial services company runs a trading platform in `us-east4` and connects to its New York data center using two Dedicated Interconnect connections in the same metropolitan area, each in a different edge availability domain. A new regulatory requirement mandates that the hybrid connection be designed to meet Google's highest published availability SLA. The on-premises team can extend circuits to a second colocation facility in another metro. What should the network engineer implement? (revised wording)
options: Add two more Dedicated Interconnect connections in the same metro, placing all four in alternating edge availability domains, with a single Cloud Router.
Keep the existing topology and add an HA VPN gateway as a backup path over the internet.

Provision four Dedicated Interconnect connections—two in each of two metros, each pair spanning both edge availability domains—use Cloud Routers in two regions, and set the VPC dynamic routing mode to global.
Replace Dedicated Interconnect with Partner Interconnect in two metros using Layer 3 partners.
questions.correct_rationale: Google's 99.99% Interconnect topology requires at least four connections across two metros (two edge availability domains per metro), Cloud Routers in two regions, and global dynamic routing so every region can use every path.
questions.distractor_summary: Two connections in one metro, regardless of how many are added there, cap out at the 99.9% topology; an HA VPN backup does not change the Interconnect SLA tier, and switching to Partner Interconnect adds provider dependency without being required.

lessons.title: How content packs stay trustworthy
body: A content pipeline lets a team publish new practice material without shipping a new app. Each pack carries a version and a checksum, so the app can tell whether it already has the update and whether the file arrived intact. Reviewers see every change by id before anything is merged, which keeps permanent ids stable and makes mistakes easy to spot.

Authors write items in their own words, validate them against the same rules the app uses, and build the pack. New items start as drafts. A reviewer approves them later and records the review date, so learners always know what has been checked by a person and what has not. Exam facts follow a stricter rule: every value cites the official page, and anything not confirmed stays empty instead of being guessed.
In practice, publish small packs often. A pack that changes a handful of items is easy to review, easy to roll back, and easy to explain in release notes.
decisions: Change it in a pack, same id
